subject: VPC reference legend + operational questions for on-prem VPC handoff
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Liu <sasha.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: VPC reference legend + operational questions for on-prem VPC handoff

Sasha — attaching the first-pass reference legend and a control/data-plane map for the private deployment we've been discussing. High-level asks/questions up front so your ops team can focus review: 

1) Egress policy: our design keeps the runtime data plane entirely in-customer VPC with a single controlled egress path for telemetry/logs to your collector (as discussed). Confirm that this path (NAT -> forwarded to 10.10.8.0/24) is acceptable.

2) Control plane reachability: control traffic (heartbeats, model registry sync, metrics) originates from the private runtime to the Redwood control plane over mTLS TLS1.3. Do you require a dedicated peering IP range or will AWS PrivateLink/ALB outbound be sufficient?

3) BGP/Peering: diagram shows an optional BGP session to your edge router for lower-latency model pull during startup. If you want this, we need ASN + BFD timers.

4) KMS & Audit: we support customer KMS for key wrapping; we will need an endpoint reachable from the private deployment to wrap/unwarp model keys during boot. We'll provide an audit evidence bundle for SOC2 — confirm retention window and preferred location for evidence exports.

Please review the attached legend (vpc-reference-legend-v1.png) — it's intentionally explicit about symbol semantics (control plane control-plane-api -> outbound TLS, data-plane sidecars -> tenant-network, telemetry -> egress-proxy). If anything is ambiguous, mark inline and I'll update.

Can we target a short sync Wed (May 29) 10–10:30am PT with your NetOps lead to align on egress & BGP?

Attachments: vpc-reference-legend-v1.png, control-data-map-v1.pdf

Thanks,
Ben
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0172

From: Sasha Liu <sasha.liu@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-escalations@acme.com
Date: 2026-05-28T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC reference legend + operational questions for on-prem VPC handoff

Ben — thanks for the diagram and clear list. Quick notes from our side (ops team reviewed):

- Egress: We prefer telemetry to be forwarded to our centralized collector at logs.acme.local (10.200.50.10). That will be NATed outbound from your runtime VPC. We need to preserve client source IPs for logging; can you confirm that your sidecar/proxy will preserve X-Forwarded-For or original IP in telemetry flows?

- Control plane: PrivateLink outbound is fine; we do ask that control-plane endpoints are in a predictable CIDR so our firewall rules can allow only those IPs. If you can supply a /27 or static set, we'll whitelist those.

- BGP: We're open to an optional BGP session, but will enforce BFD with 250ms detect timers and ASNs must be registered on our side. Our ASNs: 65099 (edge) / 65100 (backup).

- KMS: we can't expose a directly-managed KMS endpoint to third parties. We'll provide an internal wrap/unwrap proxy (details attached). The proxy requires TLS client certs; supply cert CN and we'll add to acl.

- Audit retention: SOC2 requires 12 months of telemetry-level logs accessible in read-only form; S3 with a cross-account role is preferred.

I've attached a short ops note (acme-ops-notes.docx) that lists required firewall apertures and a preferred change window (weekends). We'll take the Wed sync — can we do 10:30am PT instead (our lead has a standing meeting at 10)?

Thanks,
Sasha
Sasha Liu — NetOps Lead, Acme Payments
sasha.liu@acme.com

----
Attachments: acme-ops-notes.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Liu <sasha.liu@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC reference legend + operational questions for on-prem VPC handoff

Team / Sasha — looping in answers and actions from platform/ops side. Quoting Sasha inline where helpful.

> "We need to preserve client source IPs for logging; can you confirm your sidecar/proxy will preserve X-Forwarded-For?"
- Answer: Yes. The runtime sidecar will set X-Forwarded-For and also emit original-src as part of structured telemetry. We'll include a short JSON snippet in the runbook (see runbook-extracts-snippet.txt attached).

> "Control-plane endpoints in a predictable CIDR"
- Action: We'll provide a CIDR bundle for the control-plane egress range. For now provisional: 34.198.120.192/28 (subject to final network engineering validation). If that doesn't meet your ops constraints we'll convert to a static set via PrivateLink endpoint IPs.

> "BFD with 250ms detect timers; ASNs 65099/65100"
- Action: We can support BFD and will adopt their detect timers. Please confirm preferred hold time and desired local ASN for our side. Karthik — can you propose a local ASN and BFD hold/send timers in-line?

> "KMS proxy requiring TLS client certs"
- Action: We'll generate a client TLS cert CN per your spec and rotate it every 90 days. We need the proxy endpoint + CA bundle.

Operational to-dos: 
- Karthik: update control/data-plane diagram legend to indicate explicit egress NAT for telemetry and include the XFF/structured-telemetry call out. (target: 2026-05-29 16:00 PT)
- Marissa: generate the provisional control-plane CIDR bundle and formalize an IP allowlist doc (target: 2026-05-30)
- Ben: confirm change window preference with account team and coordinate DocuSign SOW update for pre-authorized weekend change window (target: 2026-05-30).

I'll attach the runbook snippets and a sample IAM trust policy for cross-account S3 export. Sasha — once we finalize the CIDR & ASN details we'll share a short pre-cutover checklist for NetOps signoff.

Attachments: runbook-extracts-snippet.txt

Kimberly Park
Head of Deployment Ops — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
